answer: Peers issue micro-benchmarks with wall-clock deadlines seeded by gale: each agent must finish a 45-second floating-point workload on its own hardware before the deadline, sized so one GPU cannot serve two agents at once. One honest agent spends about $0.50 of GPU time per benchmark; ten fakes must rent ten GPUs and pay $5.00 combined, so cloning costs tenfold. The beacon deadline check rejects any late or shared result, and a missed deadline slashes the bond and freezes the identity, while basalt binds the seed to this epoch so a previous run cannot be submitted twice.
